quickAnswerHtml: Keo Pla is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Surat Thani, in the downtown Surat Thani area (Talat sub-district). Budget around THB 100, and it's mostly walk-in/queue at the door

blocks.html:
Ask anyone from Surat Thani which noodle shop is the city's pride, and the name "Keo Pla" (fish wonton) on Na Mueang Road comes up almost every time. The shop never bothered with a flashy name — it sells fish wontons, so it's called Keo Pla, plain and direct, the kind of name only a place truly confident in its food would dare use. And that confidence is earned: the shop has been open for more than 60 years, passed down from parents to children, standing in the middle of downtown across from Colisseum Department Store until it became a landmark locals bring relatives and out-of-town guests to. MICHELIN Guide agrees — the restaurant has stayed listed for several years running through the 2026 edition, on the simplest recipe for good food: make everything fresh every single day, no shortcuts.

The star of the show, true to the name, is the fish wontons made fresh day by day — wonton wrappers folded around kneaded fish paste with just the right springy bite, delivering the fish's natural sweetness without needing much seasoning. The other must-order alongside it is the celery-stuffed fish roll, a hard-to-find dish this shop makes in-house and has turned into a signature. The fish roll comes in bite-sized pieces with the fragrance of celery tucked inside, and once it's blanched hot and dropped into a bowl of noodles, it works so well that plenty of people drive across town just for this one dish. It's rounded out by springy, house-made fish balls. All of it costs under 100 THB a bowl, so it's no surprise the shop has climbed to one of the top-ranked noodle restaurants in the province on Wongnai, holding an average rating of 4.3 from hundreds of real customers.

Surat Thani is the "City of Good People" that most tourists treat as nothing more than a stopover on the way to Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, even though the riverside town on the Tapi River has plenty of good food hiding in plain sight. Keo Pla is one of the best reasons to spend a night in Surat Thani before boarding the boat, because the south is fresh-seafood country, and a shop that's been turning fish into wontons, rolls, and fish balls fresh every morning for over half a century like this is real local flavor you won't find on the islands. A bowl here for breakfast before wandering the old town is how a true local starts the day.

blocks.name: Keo Pla
blocks.descHtml:
Keo Pla is one of the easiest and cheapest restaurants to visit on Surat Thani's MICHELIN list, with bowls under THB 100. Open daily 08:00-14:30, but don't count on the closing time — dishes tend to sell out before then, especially the fish wontons and celery-stuffed fish rolls, which usually run out by around 11:30. Customers pack in from mid-morning, so the safest bet is to go for breakfast or an early lunch, before noon at the latest. It's walk-in only with no advance booking, but you can call 077-282-022 to check if it's open as usual that day.

The shop is on Na Mueang Road, right in downtown Surat Thani (Talat sub-district) — the easiest landmark is that it sits across from Colisseum Department Store, just a few minutes away by car or motorbike taxi from anywhere in town. If you're catching a morning boat to Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, stopping in for breakfast beforehand is a perfect fit. Order the fish wontons, fish roll, and fish balls together in one bowl for the best value.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at Keo Pla in Surat Thani?
faq.a: No booking needed — it's walk-in only, just walk in and take a seat. But customers pack in from mid-morning, so if you want to check details or whether it's open as usual that day, call 077-282-022

faq.q: How much does a meal at Keo Pla cost?
faq.a: Very budget-friendly — bowls of noodles run under THB 100. Order the full set of fish wontons, fish rolls, and fish balls and you're still looking at just over THB 100 a person, making it one of the best-value Bib Gourmand restaurants in Surat Thani

faq.q: What should I order at Keo Pla?
faq.a: Three things you shouldn't skip: the fish wontons made fresh daily, the celery-stuffed fish rolls — the shop's hard-to-find signature — and the springy house-made fish balls. Order them together in one bowl for the fullest range of flavor

faq.q: What time does Keo Pla open, and when's the best time to go?
faq.a: Open daily 08:00-14:30, but dishes tend to sell out before closing, especially the fish wontons and fish rolls, which usually run out by around 11:30. Go for breakfast or before noon. The shop is on Na Mueang Road, downtown Surat Thani, across from Colisseum Department Store
